method: OPM data.opm.gov 'Federal Workforce Data' employment microdata (snapshot employment_202605_1, downloaded to /private/tmp/emp_202605.parquet, 2,025,993 employee-level rows) grouped by department_code + occupational_series_code + occupational_category_code (PATCO-equivalent: Professional/Administrative/Technical/Clerical/Other/Blue-Collar). Series-level exclusion lists: CLINICAL (direct-care delivery: 0602 Medical Officer, 0610 Nurse, 0620 Practical Nurse, 0621 Nursing Assistant, 0660/0661 Pharmacist/Tech, 0640 Health Aid, 0647/0644/0649/0622 allied-health technicians, 0630 Dietitian, 0633 Physical Therapist, 0185 Social Work, 0180 Psychology, 0603 Physician Assistant, plus smaller 06xx series); FRONTLINE (1802 Compliance Inspection/screening, 1801 General Inspection/CBP officers, 1895 Customs and Border Protection, 1896 Border Patrol, 1811 Criminal Investigation, 0083 Police); TRADES (occupational_category_code=B, blue-collar/wage-grade). Everything else = AI-eligible desk/knowledge work. Corroborated big structural gaps (Coast Guard active-duty military not in OPM civilian microdata; State Dept Foreign Service + Locally Employed staff not in OPM civilian microdata) against public sources per-agency below.

rows.headcount_source_title: OpenFeds (OPM FedScope, Dec 2025 Employment), corroborated by VA Workforce Dashboard Issue Thirty-One (Nov 30, 2025)
rows.headcount_quote: 451.1K employees. [VA Workforce Dashboard corroboration:] Total VA Onboard = 439,822 as of 10/31/2025, explicitly excluding 'about 10,000 intermittent, non-pay, and medical resident and trainee employees.'
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: OPM Federal Workforce Data (May 2026 snapshot, employment_202605_1) shows 445,660 VA civilian employees (department_code=VA), within 1.2% of the 451,100 official total (gap consistent with the ~10,000 intermittent/trainee employees the VA Workforce Dashboard explicitly excludes). Classified by occupational series: direct-care clinical delivery staff = 241,505 (54.2% of 445,660) -- Nurse 91,630 [0610], Medical Officer/physician 28,513 [0602], Social Work 20,341 [0185], Practical Nurse 14,261 [0620], Nursing Assistant 13,684 [0621], Pharmacist 12,485 [0660], Health Aid/Technician 8,236 [0640], Psychology 8,005 [0180], Pharmacy Technician 5,924 [0661], Diagnostic Radiologic Technologist 5,057 [0647], Medical Technologist 4,808 [0644], Medical Instrument Technician 3,785 [0649], Physical Therapist 3,214 [0633], Physician Assistant 3,102 [0603], Medical Supply Aide 3,031 [0622], Dietitian 2,915 [0630], plus ~14,500 across smaller allied-health series (speech pathology, occupational therapy, dental, optometry, podiatry, etc.). VA police (frontline, excluded) = 4,628 [0083 + small 1801/1811]. Blue-collar/trades (custodial, food service, motor vehicle, maintenance mechanics) = 30,626 (6.9%). Remaining AI-eligible desk/knowledge-work staff (Medical Support Assistants/schedulers 35,881 [0679, clerical -- these are front-desk registration/scheduling clerks with no clinical care duties, correctly counted as office-technical rather than clinical], Veterans Claims Examining 18,143 [0996], Misc Admin/Program 8,723 [0301], Management/Program Analysis 8,361 [0343], Health System Specialists (admin) 4,964 [0671], HR 7,526 [0201], IT 6,215 [2210], Medical Records Technicians (HIM coding, desk-based) 3,188 [0675], plus general/social-science researchers and other 01xx/03xx/05xx/11xx/22xx series) = 168,901. Eligible share = 168,901 / 445,660 = 0.379 -> 0.38. This is higher than the Wave-1/3 judgment-call value of 0.30 because Medical Support Assistants (the 2nd-largest single series, 35,881 people) are desk-based scheduling/registration clerks -- not 'aides on the wards' -- and are correctly reclassified as AI-eligible office-technical staff under this wave's series-level methodology rather than folded into 'clinical.'
rows.notes: Wave 4 supersedes the Wave 1/3 judgment-call eligible-share (0.30) with an OPM microdata computation. Direct-care clinical headcount (241,505, 54.2%) is large and well-documented -- flagged per task instructions as a candidate for a separate clinical-AI-use-case stratum in future work (VHA-specific tools: clinical documentation, ambient scribing, etc. are a distinct use-case class from general office productivity AI). Headcount fields carried verbatim from W3-fedscope-2026-07.json.

rows.headcount_source_title: DHS FY2026 Shutdown Contingency Plan (Procedures Relating to a Federal Lapse in Appropriations)
rows.headcount_quote: DHS estimated 249,065 of its 271,927 employees ... would be exempt and continue to work during a funding lapse.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: OPM Federal Workforce Data (May 2026 snapshot) shows only 225,578 DHS civilian employees captured (department_code=HS) -- a 46,349 gap (17%) vs. the 271,927 contingency-plan total. That gap is explained almost entirely by active-duty U.S. Coast Guard military personnel, who fall under DoD's uniformed-military personnel system rather than OPM's civilian extract: USCG reports 42,399 personnel as of Oct 31, 2025 (uscg.mil), which is uniformed/afloat and excluded as non-desk regardless. Classifying the 225,578 OPM-captured civilian staff by series: frontline/enforcement excluded = 150,040 (66.5%) -- Compliance Inspection and Support 52,109 [1802, matching TSA's own count of ~50,000 Transportation Security Officers out of ~65,000 total TSA staff per tsa.gov], General Inspection/CBP officers 34,001 [1801], Customs and Border Protection series 27,256 [1895], Border Patrol Enforcement 21,428 [1896, matching CBP's own record count of 21,471 Border Patrol agents], Criminal Investigation (ICE/HSI special agents) 13,582 [1811], Police 1,664 [0083]; blue-collar/trades = 2,145 (1.0%); clinical = 304 (0.1%, negligible). Remaining AI-eligible desk/knowledge-work staff (HQ policy/management analysts, IT 5,693 [2210], attorneys 4,108 [0905], HR, FEMA emergency-management coordination staff 9,994 [0089, treated as eligible -- primarily HQ/regional coordination and grants administration, not field first-response], intelligence analysis 1,462 [0132], contracting, budget) = 73,089. Adding the 42,399 Coast Guard military to the excluded side of the denominator: eligible share = 73,089 / 271,927 = 0.269 -> 0.27.
rows.notes: Modest upward revision from the Wave 3 judgment-call value (0.25) to a directly-computed 0.27; the two values agree closely, which corroborates both estimates. Frontline/enforcement/screening staff (TSA + CBP + Border Patrol + ICE-HSI + Coast Guard) collectively account for roughly 71% of DHS's total workforce once the uniformed Coast Guard is folded in -- by far the largest single driver of DHS's low eligible share among the five agencies in this batch. Headcount fields carried verbatim from W3-fedscope-2026-07.json.

rows.headcount_source_title: OpenFeds -- Dept. of the Treasury (OPM FedScope, December 2025 Employment)
rows.headcount_quote: Department of Treasury -- 89.9K Employees ... 2025 Separations: 28.9K (+204.2% vs 2024) ... Workforce Reduction: 32.1% of workforce separated.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: OPM Federal Workforce Data (May 2026 snapshot) shows 84,302 Treasury civilian employees (department_code=TR), about 6.2% below the 89,900 Dec-2025 OpenFeds figure -- consistent with continued IRS attrition documented by TIGTA (IRS fell from ~103,000 in Jan 2025 to an estimated 74-76,000 by early/mid-2026 per TIGTA's 'Snapshot Report: Status of the IRS's Workforce'). Classifying the 84,302 by series: frontline/enforcement excluded = 3,235 (3.8%) -- Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI special agents) 2,364 [1811], Police 405 [0083], General Inspection 404 [1801]; blue-collar/trades = 1,341 (1.6%, dominated by Bureau of Engraving and Printing production series -- Metal Forming 224, Letterpress Operating 180, Bulk Money Handling 130, Intaglio Press Operating 119); clinical = negligible (13, [1180 Psychology + minor]). Remaining AI-eligible desk/knowledge-work staff -- Contact Representative (IRS call-center, desk/computer-based) 18,897 [0962], Tax Examining (clerical processing) 10,730 [0592], Internal Revenue Agent (desk-based auditors) 7,714 [0512], IT 6,985 [2210], Misc Clerk 5,299 [0303], Financial Administration 4,291 [0501], Management/Program Analysis 3,898 [0343], attorneys 1,877 [0905], plus HR/budget/accounting/economist series -- = 79,713, i.e. 94.6% of the OPM-captured population. Treasury has essentially no direct-care clinical workforce and (since the Secret Service's 2003 transfer to DHS) a small frontline-enforcement footprint. Rounded down from the raw 0.946 parquet-composition ratio to 0.90 to be conservative about the unreconciled ~6% gap between the May-2026 parquet snapshot and the official Dec-2025 headcount, whose occupational composition is not independently verified.
rows.notes: Substantial upward revision from the Wave 1/3 judgment-call value (0.60) to a directly-computed 0.90 -- Treasury's workforce (dominated by IRS tax examining/processing/auditing plus Departmental Offices/OCC/FinCEN policy staff) is overwhelmingly desk-based; the prior judgment call appears to have significantly underweighted how office-centric IRS's non-management workforce actually is even at entry grades. Headcount fields carried verbatim from W3-fedscope-2026-07.json.

rows.headcount_source_title: RFK Jr. defends HHS tenure, 12% proposed budget cut (Healthcare Dive, Apr 2026), reporting House Appropriations subcommittee testimony
rows.headcount_quote: Kennedy said the HHS had around 62,000 employees after the layoffs, but has hired around 10,000 more since.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: OPM Federal Workforce Data (May 2026 snapshot) shows 73,186 HHS civilian employees (department_code=HE), essentially matching (and slightly exceeding) the ~72,000 Apr-2026 figure -- unlike DHS/State, there is no large structural population missing from the OPM extract. Classifying by series: direct-care clinical delivery staff excluded = 13,619 (18.6%) -- Medical Officer/physician 4,078 [0602], Nurse 4,030 [0610], Health Aid/Technician 1,317 [0640], Pharmacist 950 [0660], Medical Technologist 408 [0644], Pharmacy Technician 373 [0661], Dental Assistant 362 [0681], Nursing Assistant 284 [0621], plus smaller allied-health/dental/therapy series; frontline (OIG criminal investigation, police) = 686 (0.9%, negligible); blue-collar/trades = 1,466 (2.0%). Remaining AI-eligible desk/knowledge-work staff (NIH/CDC/FDA research scientists and policy analysts -- General Health Science 7,912 [0601], Biological Sciences 4,789 [0401], Consumer Safety/regulatory review 3,065 [0696], Chemistry/Microbiology/Pharmacology ~3,000 combined -- plus Misc Admin 4,787 [0301], Management/Program Analysis 3,673 [0343], IT 3,144 [2210], Public Health Program Specialist (admin) 3,132 [0685], Health Insurance Administration (CMS) 2,431 [0107], attorneys 858 [0905], grants management 800 [1109]) = 57,415. Eligible share = 57,415 / 73,186 = 0.7846 -> 0.78. HHS's low direct-clinical-delivery footprint (18.6%) reflects that most of the Department (NIH research, CDC public health/epidemiology, FDA regulatory review, CMS program administration, ACF/ACL/SAMHSA grants and policy) does not deliver bedside care; direct clinical care is concentrated in Indian Health Service (IHS) hospitals/clinics.
rows.notes: Large upward revision from the Wave 1/3 judgment-call value (0.55) to a directly-computed 0.78 -- flagged as needing corroboration in a future wave for one specific reason: IHS clinical care relies partly on U.S. Public Health Service Commissioned Corps officers, a uniformed personnel system analogous to Coast Guard military, which may not be fully captured in this Title-5-oriented OPM civilian extract. Since the parquet total (73,186) already matches or slightly exceeds the official headcount (72,000), there is no large unexplained population gap the way there was for DHS/State, which is reassuring, but a follow-up cross-check against IHS-specific PHS Commissioned Corps clinical strength (government-wide Corps is ~6,000 officers, majority at HHS/IHS) is recommended before treating 0.78 as final. Confidence set to medium (rather than high) for this reason despite the strong parquet/headcount reconciliation. Headcount fields carried verbatim from W3-fedscope-2026-07.json.

rows.headcount_quote: The Department of State has approximately 77,000 employees including ~14,000 Foreign Service, ~11,000 Civil Service, and ~52,000 Locally Employed Staff.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: State is not usable as a single OPM-parquet lookup like the other four agencies: the May 2026 OPM Federal Workforce Data snapshot captures only 11,370 State Dept employees (department_code=ST) -- State's domestic Civil Service, which is a Title-5 population -- while Foreign Service (a separate personnel system under the Foreign Service Act) and Locally Employed staff (non-U.S.-citizen local hires, not in any U.S. federal HR system) are entirely absent from the file. This is corroborated by the FY2023 State Dept Agency Financial Report breakdown: Foreign Service 14,039, Civil Service 12,130, Eligible Family Members (EFM) 2,188, Locally Employed Staff 50,377 (total 78,734) -- the OPM-visible 11,370 lines up closely with the AFR's 12,130 Civil Service figure. Computed per stratum: (1) Civil Service: OPM series composition for department_code=ST is 96.5% eligible (10,971/11,370 -- Passport and Visa Examining 2,009 [0967], Foreign Affairs 1,958 [0130], Misc Admin 842+1,240 [0301/0343], IT 790 [2210], HR/security/budget/legal series; clinical/frontline together <5%) -- applied to 12,130 CS = 11,705 eligible. (2) Foreign Service: ~8,500 of the 14,039 are FSOs (political/economic/consular/management/public-diplomacy generalists -- desk-based diplomatic reporting and policy work, treated as ~95% eligible = 8,075); the remaining ~5,500 are FS Specialists across 19 categories (IT, financial management, HR, office management, GSO/logistics are desk-based and eligible; Diplomatic Security special agents [~2,000-2,500, protective/investigative, excluded] and FS medical officers/PAs/nurses [excluded, clinical] pull this group down to an estimated 67% eligible = 3,685); FS total eligible = 11,760/14,039 = 0.838. (3) Eligible Family Members (2,188, work in a range of embassy support roles -- community liaison, admin, consular associate): estimated 70% eligible = 1,532. (4) Locally Employed Staff (50,377): State's own description of FSN/LE duties cites 'clerical, administrative, technical, fiscal support' alongside specific manual/support roles (vehicle drivers, mailroom, switchboard operators), and many posts maintain sizable Local Guard Force and facilities/maintenance staffs; in the absence of a public occupational breakdown for this population, estimated conservatively at 45% eligible (a low-confidence judgment call) = 22,670. Weighted total: (11,705+11,760+1,532+22,670) / (12,130+14,039+2,188+50,377) = 47,667/78,734 = 0.605 -> 0.61.
rows.notes: State has no Wave-3 row (Wave-3/fedscope-2026-07 did not cover State), so total_headcount/headcount_as_of/headcount_source_url/headcount_source_title/headcount_quote are carried forward unchanged from Wave-1 (W1-C.json) rather than refreshed -- a headcount refresh against the FY2023 AFR figures (78,734 total) or a newer AFR is recommended for a future wave. ai_eligible_share is a modest downward revision from the Wave-1 judgment call (0.65) to 0.61; the two are close, but this wave's figure rests on much shakier ground than VA/DHS/Treasury/HHS because only the ~12,130-person Civil Service stratum (15% of the Department) is directly measured from OPM microdata -- the Foreign Service and (especially) Locally Employed Staff eligible-rates are public-description-informed estimates, not counted compositions, and confidence is capped at medium for that reason. The Locally Employed Staff eligible-rate (45%) is the single weakest input and the best candidate for follow-up research (a GAO or State OIG report breaking down LE staff duty/position codes would meaningfully sharpen this).
